title.narrative: Decent & Green Jobs Work in the Agriculture, Agro-processing, & Food Security Sector in Kenya 2018-

description.narrative:
Economic development and job creation are key components of poverty alleviation. In fact, employment is a central priority for both people living in poverty, and for governments and donors attempting to have strong development impact. At this point in history, however, we face a dual challenge, both social and ecological, and there is just no are not the time nor the resources to respond to this challenge in a non-integrated way.
Laudato Si highlights that our priority is therefore to respond to both the cry of the poor and the cry of the earth. When considering the unemployment and underemployment challenges that countries around the world are currently facing, our priority is, therefore, to call for decent, green jobs for all.
Jesuit Hakimani (JH) and CAFOD would like to explore what this means in the Kenyan context: What are decent, green jobs in Kenya… why are these important… and what do decision makers need to do to support the creation of decent and green jobs?
Research Objectives:
1. Investigate the gaps about global contemporary concerns & considerations in the current policy framework on job creation that are decent, green & sustainable. 2. Consolidate and provide relevant improvements at the county and at the national level in the policy and legal framework so as to create decent, green & sustainable jobs. 3. Identify connection and to raise awareness amongst rural farmers and the general public of the connection between bad governance and persistent food insecurity in Kenya. 4. To capture and solidify the public sentiments and awaken social thinking on issues of governance, decent, green jobs, & food security especially amongst the rural poor and urban working poor.
